name: Twinflame Tyrant
oracle_text:
Flying
If a source you control would deal damage to an opponent or a permanent an opponent controls, it deals double that damage instead.
blocked_sentences: If a source you control would deal damage to an opponent or a permanent an opponent controls, it deals double that damage instead.

needs.what: A recipient-side PLAYER filter on the `replace_damage` static -- `affects_player: "opponent"` (with "you"/"any" for the family's other sentences) accepted by the loader on this effect and, crucially, READ by `player_statics.damage_multiplier` (src/automtg/engine/player_statics.py line 1178) on the branch where the damage is going to a player. That function is called from two places: `primitives.damage_player` (src/automtg/engine/primitives.py line 391) with `target_oid=None`, and `primitives.damage_permanent` (line 585) with the permanent's oid. Today the `None` case can only be reached by a static with NO `affects` at all, so the recipient side is all-or-nothing. It needs, in one static, the printed OR: this damage is doubled if the recipient is a player matching `affects_player` OR a permanent matching `affects`. Two filters that currently AND (both must pass when both are written) have to become a union when the new key is present, because a single damage event is dealt either to a player or to a permanent and can never satisfy both -- ANDing them would double nothing at all. With that key the card is exactly `{"effect": "replace_damage", "damage_multiplier": 2, "affects_player": "opponent", "affects": {"controller": "opponent"}}` and no `combat_only`. It unlocks the whole opponent-facing doubler family beside this card -- Angrath's Marauders, Gratuitous Violence's opponent-side cousins, Torbran-shaped 'damage to opponents' riders -- none of which can name a player as the thing being hit.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `affects` is the only recipient filter `replace_damage` has, and it is permanent-only by construction: `damage_multiplier`'s own docstring says "a static carrying an `affects` filter never applies then: a player is not a permanent", and the code backs it -- `state.objects.get(target_oid)` with `target_oid=None` yields `None` and the static is skipped (src/automtg/engine/player_statics.py lines 1215-1219). So `affects: {"controller": "opponent"}` implements only the second half of the printed line and silently drops every point of damage aimed at the opponent themself, which is the half this card is played for. Dropping `affects` instead is worse and wrong in both directions: it is Furnace of Rath restricted to your sources, doubling your Pyroclasm onto your own board, your fight damage onto your own creature, and the damage your own City of Brass / Mana Crypt deals to YOU -- strictly stronger than printed on offense and strictly worse on defense. `affects_player` is not a workaround either: `replace_damage` is deliberately NOT in `PLAYER_WIDE_STATIC_EFFECTS` (src/automtg/cards/loader/vocabulary.py line 464, with the comment "Filtered on **both ends**, which is why it is not one of the five player-wide multipliers"), and the loader's replace_damage branch (src/automtg/cards/loader/__init__.py lines 2475-2503) never rejects the key, while the compile loop copies it onto the static unconditionally (line 2941). Written today it would LOAD CLEAN and be read by nothing -- a silent no-op, which is the worst of the three outcomes. `replace_life_loss` with `loss_multiplier` is the nearest player-wide relative and is genuinely a different sentence: damage is not life loss -- it is marked on creatures, feeds deathtouch and infect, and only incidentally lowers a life total -- so it cannot double the permanent half of this line at all. And no trigger substitutes: this is a replacement ('would deal ... instead'), so `deals_damage_to_player`/`dealt_damage` fire after the undoubled damage has already landed, which neither makes a lethal hit lethal nor doubles damage onto a creature that is already dead.

needs.what: A `damage_source` filter that can match a source which is not a permanent on the battlefield -- "a source YOU CONTROL" covers the spells you cast, tokens, emblems and abilities on the stack, not just your creatures. Concretely: `damage_multiplier` resolves the dealer through `characteristics._matches` (src/automtg/engine/characteristics.py line 1375), which returns False for any object where `obj.on_battlefield` is false (line 1388-1389), and `op_damage`'s dealer defaults to `ctx.source_oid` (src/automtg/engine/effects/ops_life.py line 178), the resolving SPELL object for a burn spell. So the engine needs either a controller-only source test that is answered off the object's controller regardless of zone, or a dedicated `damage_source: {"controller": "you"}` path in `damage_multiplier` that consults the source's controller before `_matches` refuses it on zone. This is shared with Fiery Emancipation and Dictate of the Twin Gods-style 'a source you control' doublers, all of which are about burn spells first and creatures second.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `damage_source` is validated against STATIC_FILTER_KEYS (src/automtg/cards/loader/__init__.py line 2495) and matched by the static filter language, whose entry condition is 'is this object on the battlefield'. `{"controller": "you"}` therefore reads as 'a permanent you control' and quietly misses every instant and sorcery you cast -- the doubler that does not double your Lightning Bolt is not the printed card. Omitting `damage_source` reaches spells, but then it reaches the OPPONENT's sources too, doubling their burn and their attackers against them, which no printed card says. There is no third filter site: `grant_ability`'s `affects` is validated against the same STATIC_FILTER_KEYS (src/automtg/cards/loader/statics.py), so 'sources you control have <replace_damage>' cannot name a spell either, and the effect-side selector language is never consulted by `damage_multiplier`.

notes: Deliberately not written as a partial answer: `flying` is already in the packet's starting_point, and a card carrying only that keyword leaves the second printed line unclaimed and fails the residual gate. The first need is the blocking one and is the cheaper of the two -- one key accepted on the replace_damage branch, one union-shaped check in `damage_multiplier`'s player path; the second need decides whether the card doubles your burn spells as printed or only your permanents. Once both exist the sandbox expectation is `{"zone": "battlefield", "battlefield_count": 33}`: the harness casts the Dragon and stops, combat is declined and nothing in that position deals damage, so the replacement itself cannot be observed there.
